correctness.rationale: For 0<T<1 an unsecured vertex is safe exactly when its unsecured component has no edges; NE unsecured sets are precisely maximal independent sets, and social optima leave maximum independent sets. Thus BestNE=n-alpha, WorstNE=n-i, Opt=n-alpha. For the two k-leaf hubs bridged at a1b1, a three-edge matching and explicit size-3 vertex cover prove alpha(G_k)=alpha(H_k)=2k-1, so opt/bestNE=3. Hubs form independent dominating set in tree G_k and no universal vertex exists, so i(G_k)=2. With added uv, case split on which hubs are in an independent dominating set forces >=k+1, attained by one hub plus all opposite leaves, so i(H_k)=k+1. n<=5 connected graph has i<=2; if i=1 universal persists; hence six-vertex sharpness. Independently enumerated all vertex subsets for k=2,3,4, confirming (alpha,i)=(3,2)->(3,3),(5,2)->(5,4),(7,2)->(7,5). Finite cases do not establish unbounded k.
